# Solution circuits

<!-- GENERATED by data/build_circuits.py from data/circuits.yaml. Edit the YAML, then rebuild. -->

A solution circuit is a set of different kinds of organization that have been used together on one problem. Community land trusts hold land, unions organize labor, credit unions lend. The question this page tries to answer is which combinations have a track record, what went wrong when they were tried, and where the directory can find the pieces.

Read this before using it:

- **A circuit is a pattern, not a partnership.** Nothing here says that any two listed organizations know each other or want to work together.
- **Evidence is graded.** "Combination documented" means the sources show these kinds of organization working together. "Parts documented separately" means each part has evidence but the combination does not. "Hypothesis" means no precedent has been checked.
- **Every circuit lists what went wrong.** The limits are part of the evidence. Several of the best-known examples have closed, converted or lost funding.
- **Sources were opened by an automated research pass on the date shown, and have not been re-checked by a person.** If a link no longer says what is quoted, please correct `data/circuits.yaml`.
- **Coverage is counts of rule matches.** It comes from the public release dated 2026-04-27 (158,715 rows). A match is a research lead; see [Role rules](#role-rules) for how accurate each rule looked in a sample.

To try one, open the [map](https://commonweave.earth/map.html#view=list), pick the goal, choose a country and city, and select candidates for each role yourself. The method and its limits are in the [operating model](FRAMEWORK-OPERATING-MODEL.md).

## Labor-for-housing pipeline

**Goal on the map:** Build permanently affordable homes with organized labor  
**Evidence:** Combination documented. Unions have sponsored cooperative housing at scale in several countries. None of the sources shows a union working with a community land trust specifically, so that pairing is still a proposal (see LABOR-FOR-HOUSING-GUIDE.md).

Homes that stay affordable need land held outside the speculative market, skilled construction labor, residents who govern the result, and patient finance. No single kind of organization holds all four.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find organized labor (labor union) | Ask whether the local or its trades council has a housing committee, apprenticeship program, or pension capital it can direct. | 842 | 506 |
| Hold the land in trust (community land trust) | Ask about resale rules, who sits on the board, and whether it can take on new parcels. | 774 | 71 |
| Organize build labor and training (self-build or sweat-equity housing program) | Ask how resident hours are credited, supervised and insured. | 428 | 52 |
| Plan resident ownership (housing cooperative or cohousing group) | Ask how members govern, and what stops a later vote to sell at market price. | 1,158 | 216 |
| Find patient finance (credit union or cooperative lender) | Ask whether it lends on leasehold or limited-equity homes. | 188 | 11 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Amalgamated Housing Cooperative** (New York, United States). Sponsored by the Amalgamated Clothing Workers union; the first 303 households moved in on 1 November 1927. [Source](https://amalgamated-bronx.coop/?p=7), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Riksbyggen** (Sweden). Established on the initiative of the building workers' unions during a housing shortage; it reports about 1,700 housing associations under management. [Source](https://www.riksbyggen.se/om-riksbyggen/about-us/), checked 2026-11-26.
- **FUCVAM mutual-aid housing cooperatives** (Uruguay). Cooperatives with collective ownership, built largely by members' own labor and rooted in the trade-union movement. The transfer of the model won a World Habitat Award in 2012. [Source](https://world-habitat.org/world-habitat-awards/winners-and-finalists/south-south-cooperation-international-transfer-of-the-fucvam-model-of-mutual-aid-housing-cooperatives/), checked 2026-11-26.
- **AFL-CIO Housing Investment Trust** (United States). A fixed-income fund of about $7.6 billion with a 100% union labor requirement for on-site construction; it reports 133,429 housing and healthcare units financed since 1984. Figures are self-reported. [Source](https://www.aflcio-hit.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/3Q26-HIT-Factsheet.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Co-operative Housing Foundation of Canada** (Canada). Founded in 1968 by the Canadian Labour Congress, the Co-operative Union of Canada and the Canadian Union of Students; about 2,000 housing co-ops followed, until federal financing of new projects stopped in the early 1990s. [Source](https://www.thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/housing-co-operatives), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- Co-op City, built by the union-backed United Housing Foundation, went through a thirteen-month rent strike that destroyed the Foundation and nearly bankrupted the state housing finance agency. [Source](https://www.gothamcenter.org/blog/after-the-rent-strike-neoliberalism-and-co-op-city).
- Neue Heimat, the West German union-owned housing group that built more than 460,000 apartments, collapsed after a public scandal in 1982. [Source](https://www.tum.de/en/about-tum/news/press-releases/details/35274/).
- Seward Park Cooperative, a union-sponsored limited-equity co-op, voted in 1995 to become a full-equity co-op and lifted its price ceilings over five years. Penn South voted the other way and stayed limited-equity. [Source](https://sewardparkcoop.com/spc_history.html).
- Electchester, built by an electrical workers' local, has been described by a housing historian as a homogeneous and exclusive enclave. [Source](https://urbanomnibus.net/2013/12/electchester-a-city-made-for-workers/).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- Public land, zoning and subsidy decisions made by local government.

**What would count against it:** If a search of union-sponsored housing in three countries finds that most projects converted to market-rate resale or failed financially within 40 years, the circuit should be described as a way to build homes, not to keep them affordable.

**Directory coverage:** 3 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 1,722 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, DE, GB, US.

Cities with the most candidates per role, as leads for a closer look: Chicago, IL (US); Richmond, VA (US); Phoenix, AZ (US).

**Related open problems:** [land-transition](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#land-transition), [power-transfer](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#power-transfer)

## Tenant purchase and anti-displacement pipeline

**Goal on the map:** Help tenants stay, or buy their building  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

Preventing displacement takes organized tenants, legal capacity to use the rights they have, and an owner that will keep the building affordable after purchase.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find organized tenants (tenant or resident organization) | Ask whether a tenant association exists in the building or neighbourhood and what it has already tried. | 21 | 4 |
| Find legal capacity (legal aid or community law centre) | Ask about eligibility, current caseload and whether it takes eviction or purchase cases. | 267 | 13 |
| Find a long-term owner (community land trust) | Ask whether it can acquire occupied buildings and on what terms. | 774 | 71 |
| Find a development partner (nonprofit affordable-housing developer) | Ask about experience with tenant purchases and how tenants keep a say. | 1,588 | 12 |
| Find acquisition finance (credit union or cooperative lender) | Ask how quickly it can commit funds inside a legal purchase window. | 188 | 11 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act** (Washington DC, United States). A study commissioned by the city housing department found 16,224 affordable units developed or preserved through the law. [Source](https://cnhed.org/news/cnhed-releases-comprehensive-analysis-of-dcs-tenant-opportunity-to-purchase-act-topa/), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Right to counsel in eviction cases** (New York City, United States). In fiscal year 2025, 83% of fully represented households were allowed to remain. That category includes households given extra time to move, so it is not the same as avoiding eviction. [Source](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/hra/downloads/pdf/services/civiljustice/OCJ_Annual_Report_2025.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Dudley Neighbors Inc.** (Boston, United States). A resident-created land trust that reports more than 30 acres of community-controlled land and 228 housing units, including rental, ownership and co-op homes. [Source](https://www.dudleyneighborsinc.org/), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- In 95% of Washington DC transactions with a tenant association, tenants assigned their purchase rights and did not buy; the process can delay sales by up to 420 days. [Source](https://www.dcpolicycenter.org/publications/topas-promise-and-pitfalls-in-dc/).
- New York's citywide representation rate fell from 71% in fiscal 2021 to 42% in fiscal 2024, with legal-service attrition of 20-55% a year. [Source](https://comptroller.nyc.gov/reports/evictions-up-representation-down/).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- A law that gives tenants a purchase right or a right to counsel. Without one, the legal role has little to enforce.

**What would count against it:** If tenant purchase laws in two or more cities show that fewer than one building in ten ends in resident or nonprofit ownership, describe this as an eviction-delay circuit and drop the purchase claim.

**Directory coverage:** 1 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 1,428 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, US.

Cities with the most candidates per role, as leads for a closer look: Worcester, MA (US).

**Related open problems:** [land-transition](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#land-transition), [power-transfer](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#power-transfer)

## Housing First partnership

**Goal on the map:** Move people from homelessness into stable housing  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

People leaving long-term homelessness need a tenancy first and voluntary support around it. That takes outreach, a landlord willing to house without preconditions, and health support.

> **Care needed.** People using these services are at risk from exposure. Work with organizations, never with client details.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find outreach (homelessness outreach or shelter) | Ask who they reach, and how referrals are made with consent. | 101 | 45 |
| Find homes (nonprofit affordable-housing developer) | Ask whether tenancies are offered without treatment or sobriety conditions. | 1,588 | 12 |
| Find health and recovery support (mental health or addiction service) | Ask whether support is voluntary and continues after move-in. | 1,656 | 308 |
| Find primary care (community clinic or health centre) | Ask about access for people without documents or a fixed address. | 900 | 20 |

**Where it has been done**

- **At Home / Chez Soi randomized trial** (Canada (five cities)). Among 2,148 participants, 62% of those given Housing First were housed all of the time in the last six months, against 31% receiving usual services. [Source](https://mentalhealthcommission.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/At2520Home2520Final2520Report2520-2520Exec2520Summary2520-2520ENG_0.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- The same trial found mental health and substance use improved by a similar amount in both groups. A 2019 systematic review found housing stability improved but most health effects were imprecisely estimated. [Source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6581117/).
- Finland, the usual national example, reported about 4,579 homeless people in 2025, a 20% rise that the Y-Foundation attributes to benefit cuts. Gains depend on continued public funding. [Source](https://ysaatio.fi/en/housing-first/homelessness-in-finland/).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- Rent subsidy or social housing allocation from government.

**What would count against it:** If local data show fewer than half of housed participants still housed after two years, the local version is not delivering the trial result and should be reviewed before more referrals.

**Directory coverage:** 7 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 2,039 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, GB, US.

City-level coverage is not published for this circuit because the work involves people at risk.

**Related open problems:** [partial-abundance](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#partial-abundance)

## Worker ownership transition

**Goal on the map:** Keep jobs when a firm closes or its owner retires  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

When a viable firm is about to close, the workers can sometimes buy it. They need to be organized, advised on structure, and financed quickly.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find the organized workforce (labor union) | Ask whether the union has handled a closure or buyout and what members want. | 842 | 506 |
| Find conversion advice (cooperative developer, federation or support network) | Ask about feasibility studies, legal structure and how many conversions it has completed. | 581 | 90 |
| Find buyout finance (credit union or cooperative lender) | Ask what it lends without personal guarantees. | 188 | 11 |
| Find management and skills training (workforce training or apprenticeship provider) | Ask whether training covers governance and finance for new worker-owners. | 142 | 5 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Marcora Law worker buyouts** (Italy). Researchers tracked 257 worker buyouts to the end of 2014; 131 were still active. Of 81 started after the 2001 reform, 10 had closed. [Source](https://geo.coop/sites/default/files/2021-07/ItalyWBOReport-15_17RapportoVietaDepedriCarrano.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.
- **USW-Mondragon union co-op model** (United States). The United Steelworkers and Mondragon signed an agreement in 2009 to promote union co-ops; a 2017 study counted eleven US initiatives applying the model and described both possibilities and dilemmas. [Source](https://cleo.rutgers.edu/articles/stronger-together-the-usw-mondragon-union-co-op-model/), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Worker-managed firms in Uruguay** (Uruguay). The hazard of dissolution was 29% lower for worker-managed firms than for conventional firms, after excluding microenterprises. [Source](https://ideas.repec.org/a/sae/ilrrev/v67y2014i1p202-238.html), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- About half of all Italian buyouts ever tracked had closed by 2014. The high survival figure applies only to the post-2001 cohort. [Source](https://geo.coop/sites/default/files/2021-07/ItalyWBOReport-15_17RapportoVietaDepedriCarrano.pdf).
- When Mondragon's Fagor Electrodomésticos closed in 2013, worker-members lost capital and savings. Three years on, 92% had a solution (relocation, early retirement or new work) and 8% remained unemployed. [Source](https://cleo.rutgers.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Inter-Cooperation-Mechanisms-in-Mondragon-Managing-the-Crisis-of-Fagor-ElectrodomEsticos.pdf).
- The US Main Street Employee Ownership Act of 2018 did not remove the personal-guarantee barrier; the Small Business Administration said it would not move forward with an alternative. [Source](https://us.coop/blog/new-sba-report-on-financing-alternatives-does-not-fulfill-congresss-directive-in-main-street-employee-ownership-act/).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- A legal right for workers to be told before a sale, and public co-investment such as Italy's.

**What would count against it:** If a review of conversions in a country without Marcora-style co-investment finds fewer than half survive five years, the circuit depends on the law and should not be offered as a local remedy on its own.

**Directory coverage:** 0 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 746 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, BR, GB, KE, US.

**Related open problems:** [tipping-point](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#tipping-point), [power-transfer](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#power-transfer), [developing-nations](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#developing-nations)

## Care work with a union and a stake

**Goal on the map:** Make care jobs sustainable for the people doing them  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

Home care and similar work is essential, poorly paid and has very high turnover. Worker ownership and collective bargaining are two routes to better jobs; a few organizations combine them.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find care providers and carers' groups (home-care provider or carers' organization) | Ask about pay, hours, turnover and whether workers have a say. | 119 | 60 |
| Find worker representation (labor union) | Ask which union organizes care workers locally and what it has bargained. | 842 | 506 |
| Explore worker ownership (cooperative developer, federation or support network) | Ask whether it has supported a care co-op and how it was financed. | 581 | 90 |
| Find training (workforce training or apprenticeship provider) | Ask whether training is paid and leads to higher wages. | 142 | 5 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Cooperative Home Care Associates** (New York, United States). A worker cooperative founded in 1985 whose workers unionized with 1199SEIU in 2003. Its turnover has been reported as lower than at comparable agencies. It now employs over 1,600 people. [Source](https://cleo.rutgers.edu/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/CASE-STUDY-CHCA.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Self Employed Women's Association** (India). A trade union registered in 1972 that has also promoted more than 100 member-owned cooperatives, federated in a separate body. [Source](https://www.ilo.org/resource/article/sewa-cooperative-federation-india-towards-self-reliance), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- Just under half of Cooperative Home Care Associates' workers are members, a share that fell as it absorbed other agencies. Its income depends on public reimbursement rates. [Source](https://cleo.rutgers.edu/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/CASE-STUDY-CHCA.pdf).
- Japan's Fureai Kippu time-credit schemes for eldercare declined after public long-term care insurance began in 2000, and there are no statistics on participants or hours. Volunteer credit did not replace paid care. [Source](https://www.ijccr.net/article/view/9150).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- Public payers that set reimbursement rates, which largely determine care wages.

**What would count against it:** This circuit tests FALSIFIERS.md F-FW-2 from the other side. If unionized care co-ops show turnover no lower than conventional agencies paying the same wage, ownership adds nothing beyond pay.

**Directory coverage:** 1 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 711 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, BR, GB, US.

Cities with the most candidates per role, as leads for a closer look: Oakland, CA (US).

**Related open problems:** [unglamorous-work](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#unglamorous-work), [partial-abundance](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#partial-abundance)

## Anchor procurement and community wealth

**Goal on the map:** Keep institutional spending in the local economy  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

Hospitals, universities and councils buy large volumes of goods and services. Redirecting part of that to local and worker-owned suppliers needs a willing buyer, a supplier able to deliver, and finance to start or convert firms.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find a large local buyer (anchor institution (hospital, university, public body)) | Ask what it buys locally now and which contracts are coming up. | 1,785 | 60 |
| Find or start a worker-owned supplier (worker cooperative) | Ask what it can supply at the volume and standard required. | 172 | 7 |
| Find business development support (cooperative developer, federation or support network) | Ask whether it has prepared firms for institutional contracts. | 581 | 90 |
| Find start-up finance (credit union or cooperative lender) | Ask how much of the start-up cost can be equity or grant, not debt. | 188 | 11 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Preston community wealth building** (Preston, United Kingdom). Six anchor institutions' spending with Preston-based businesses rose from £37 million (5%) in 2012/13 to over £112 million (18.2%) in 2016/17, while their total spending fell. [Source](https://www.councils.coop/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Community-Wealth-Building-Preston-City-Council.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Evergreen Cooperatives** (Cleveland, United States). Launched in 2008 by a working group including the Cleveland Foundation, Cleveland Clinic, University Hospitals and Case Western Reserve University to build worker-owned suppliers. [Source](https://evgoh.com/about), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- A policy review concluded there is little evidence on the impact of community wealth building, and that not all local improvement can be attributed to the Preston model. [Source](https://wcpp.org.uk/blog-posts/the-preston-model-a-panacea-for-wales/).
- The first Evergreen businesses were entirely debt financed, which made profitability very difficult, and key decisions were made before worker-owners were included. [Source](https://geo.coop/blog/critical-look-evergreen-model).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- Procurement law and the anchor's own purchasing rules.

**What would count against it:** If local spending rises but local wages and employment do not move relative to comparable towns over five years, the circuit shifts invoices without building wealth.

**Directory coverage:** 0 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 1,404 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: BR, DE, GB, US.

**Related open problems:** [power-transfer](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#power-transfer), [nation-states](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#nation-states)

## Community health mesh

**Goal on the map:** Reach people that clinics miss  
**Evidence:** Parts documented separately. The clinic plus community-health-worker pairing has trial evidence. The sources do not show mutual aid networks formally joined to it.

Clinics treat the people who arrive. Community health workers and neighbourhood groups reach people who do not, and connect them to care.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find a clinic (community clinic or health centre) | Ask who is eligible, what it costs and whether it accepts outside referrals. | 900 | 20 |
| Find community health workers (community health worker or health-education group) | Ask whether workers are paid, how they are supervised and which neighbourhoods they cover. | 642 | 8 |
| Find neighbourhood networks (neighbourhood mutual aid network) | Ask whether the group is still active and wants health referrals at all. | 5,164 | 4,911 |

**Where it has been done**

- **IMPaCT community health worker program** (Philadelphia, United States). An economic analysis estimated a return of $2.47 to an average Medicaid payer for every dollar invested within the fiscal year. [Source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8564553/), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- The return estimate rests on differences in hospital use that were not statistically significant in the underlying trial (for example 31.6% against 23.3% hospitalized, p = 0.11). [Source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8564553/).
- Many mutual aid groups in the directory were listed during the 2020 pandemic response and may no longer be active. [Source](https://github.com/simonlpaige/commonweave/blob/master/docs/DATA-AUDIT-2026-09-05.md).

**What would count against it:** If paid community health workers attached to a clinic produce no measurable change in missed appointments or avoidable admissions after a year, the outreach role is not adding to clinical care in that setting.

**Directory coverage:** 63 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 1,378 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, GB, US.

Cities with the most candidates per role, as leads for a closer look: Los Angeles, CA (US); Boston, MA (US); Portland, OR (US); Chicago, IL (US); Seattle, WA (US); Phoenix, AZ (US); Miami, FL (US); Charlotte, NC (US); Baltimore, MD (US); Philadelphia, PA (US); San Francisco, CA (US); Albuquerque, NM (US).

## Non-police crisis response

**Goal on the map:** Send health responders to mental health and welfare calls  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

Many emergency calls concern mental distress, intoxication or homelessness. A health-led response needs trained responders, a route into ongoing care, and a place in the emergency dispatch system.

> **Care needed.** Never record or share details about people in crisis.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find crisis and mental health responders (mental health or addiction service) | Ask about hours of cover, training and what they do not handle. | 1,656 | 308 |
| Find follow-up care (community clinic or health centre) | Ask whether it accepts handovers from a crisis team. | 900 | 20 |
| Find shelter and outreach (homelessness outreach or shelter) | Ask about night-time capacity and how handovers work. | 101 | 45 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Support Team Assisted Response (STAR)** (Denver, United States). A six-month pilot was associated with a 34% fall in reports of targeted, less serious crimes and no detectable effect on more serious crimes. [Source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9176742), checked 2026-11-26.
- **CAHOOTS** (Eugene, United States). A clinic-run mobile crisis service that operated for decades inside the city's emergency system. A police analysis put the true diversion rate at roughly 5-8% of calls, lower than commonly reported. [Source](https://csgjusticecenter.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/CAHOOTS-Program-Analysis.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- CAHOOTS stopped serving Eugene in April 2025 because the parties lacked the financial capacity to continue. A long track record did not protect it from a funding gap. [Source](https://opb.org/article/2025/04/08/cahoots-service-ending-in-eugene-effective-immediately).
- The Denver study was quasi-experimental; its authors note part of the drop is mechanical because health responders are less likely to record people as offenders. [Source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9176742).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- The public emergency dispatch centre and the budget that pays responders. Community organizations cannot substitute for either.

**What would count against it:** If a local service cannot secure multi-year public funding, treat it as a pilot. The Eugene closure is the reference case.

**Directory coverage:** 8 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 1,432 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, BR, GB, US.

City-level coverage is not published for this circuit because the work involves people at risk.

## Community safety and repair

**Goal on the map:** Reduce violence and repair harm without relying only on prison  
**Evidence:** Parts documented separately. Each part has its own evaluations, some with null results. No source shows the parts run together as one local system.

Reducing repeat harm takes several things at once, namely a way for the people involved to address what happened, paid work and support after prison, and local organizations that keep young people connected.

> **Care needed.** This work involves survivors and people leaving prison. Use organizational information only, and do not publish participant details.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find restorative and mediation practice (mediation or restorative-justice organization) | Ask which kinds of harm it handles, and how survivors consent. | 146 | 46 |
| Find re-entry support (re-entry or post-prison support organization) | Ask how soon after release people can enrol. | 92 | 0 |
| Find paid transitional work (workforce training or apprenticeship provider) | Ask whether jobs are paid from day one and what follows them. | 142 | 5 |
| Find violence-prevention and survivor support (community violence-prevention or survivor-support group) | Ask how it works with, or keeps distance from, police. | 74 | 20 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Restorative justice conferencing (systematic review)** (Australia, United Kingdom, United States). Across ten randomized trials, conferences produced a modest but cost-effective reduction in repeat offending and higher victim satisfaction. All cases had consent from both parties before randomization. [Source](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:wly:camsys:v:9:y:2013:i:1:p:1-59), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Center for Employment Opportunities** (New York, United States). A randomized evaluation found 16-22% reductions in recidivism among people who enrolled within three months of release. Employment gains faded over time. [Source](https://www.mdrc.org/work/publications/more-job), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Local nonprofits and the crime decline** (United States (264 cities)). Every 10 additional organizations focused on crime and community life per 100,000 residents was associated with a 9% drop in murder. This is an instrumental-variables estimate, not an experiment. [Source](https://inequality.stanford.edu/node/9575), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- The READI Chicago randomized trial of jobs plus cognitive behavioural therapy found no statistically significant change in its primary index of serious violence after 20 months. [Source](https://www.nber.org/papers/w30852).
- A review of violence-interruption programs judged the evidence mixed at best, meriting the label promising and not effective. [Source](https://jeffreybutts.net/2014/12/30/arph2015/).
- Restorative conferencing evidence covers willing parties. It says nothing about cases where a survivor or the person responsible refuses. [Source](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:wly:camsys:v:9:y:2013:i:1:p:1-59).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- Courts and prosecutors, who decide whether a case can be diverted at all.

**What would count against it:** If a city with all four roles active shows no difference in repeat-harm rates from a matched city without them over five years, the parts do not add up to a system.

**Directory coverage:** 0 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 306 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, US.

City-level coverage is not published for this circuit because the work involves people at risk.

**Related open problems:** [prisons](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#prisons), [historical-wrongs](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#historical-wrongs)

## Local food security loop

**Goal on the map:** Connect growers, a food hub and food access  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

A local food system needs growers, a channel that aggregates and sells what they grow, and organizations that get food to people who cannot pay market prices.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find growers (community grower or small-farm group) | Ask what they grow, in what volume and season. | 2,251 | 74 |
| Find a cooperative channel (food cooperative, hub or market) | Ask about minimum volumes, food safety requirements and who it sells to. | 34 | 16 |
| Find food access (food bank or free-food program) | Ask whether it can accept fresh produce and how it is funded. | 2,202 | 91 |

**Where it has been done**

- **United States food hubs** (United States). In the 2025 national survey, 65% of food hubs sold to schools or food banks, so the grower-hub-access chain is common practice. [Source](https://rmfu.org/wp-content/uploads/National-Food-Hub-Survey-Report-2025Final1-1.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- In the same survey more than half of hubs were highly dependent on grants, the largest share in six survey rounds, and public purchasing programs were cancelled in March 2025. [Source](https://rmfu.org/wp-content/uploads/National-Food-Hub-Survey-Report-2025Final1-1.pdf).
- The directory has very few food hubs or food co-ops (34 release records match the rule), so the middle role will usually look empty. [Source](https://github.com/simonlpaige/commonweave/blob/master/SOLUTION-CIRCUITS.md).

**What would count against it:** If a local loop cannot cover its distribution costs without grants after three years, it is a subsidized service. That may still be worth funding, but it should be described that way.

**Directory coverage:** 1 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 2,988 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, BR, CA, US.

Cities with the most candidates per role, as leads for a closer look: Saint Paul, MN (US).

| Find growing space (community grower or small-farm group) | Ask whether it wants compost and can check its quality. | 2,251 | 74 |

**What would count against it:** If no documented case of the three working together can be found and source-checked, remove this circuit.

## Land stewardship alliance

**Goal on the map:** Keep land healthy and in use  
**Evidence:** Parts documented separately. The strongest evidence is for secure Indigenous and community tenure. The sources do not test this three-role combination.

Land protected without people using it is hard to maintain; land used without stewardship degrades. Secure community tenure, ecological monitoring and working use together are associated with better outcomes.

> **Care needed.** Land defenders and Indigenous communities can be endangered by visibility. Indigenous nations are rights-holders and governments, not a role to be slotted into someone else's plan. Approach them on their terms or not at all.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find ecological stewards (conservation or watershed steward) | Ask what they monitor and whether they share data. | 735 | 180 |
| Find working land users (community grower or small-farm group) | Ask about tenure, and which practices they would change with secure access. | 2,251 | 74 |
| Find community land holders (community land trust) | Ask whether the trust holds farmland or open land as well as housing. | 774 | 71 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Titling of Indigenous communities** (Peruvian Amazon). Titling reduced forest clearing by more than three-quarters and disturbance by roughly two-thirds in the two years around the award of title. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5402456/), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Indigenous Protected Areas and rangers** (Australia). A government-commissioned review of five areas valued outcomes at $96.5 million for $35.2 million invested. It monetizes stakeholder-reported outcomes and is not an ecological measurement. [Source](https://www.niaa.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/publications/SROI-Consolidated-Report-IPA_1.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Community ownership of land** (Scotland). At December 2025, 554 community groups owned 214,883 hectares, 2.8% of Scotland's land. 72% of that area is in the Western Isles. [Source](https://www.gov.scot/publications/community-ownership-in-scotland-2025/pages/key-points/), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- The Peruvian result is short-term by the authors' own account. Canada's evaluation of its Indigenous Guardians initiative found a need to improve data collection to demonstrate results. [Source](https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/corporate/transparency/priorities-management/evaluations/evaluation-eccc-indigenous-guardians-initiative-2024/at-a-glance.html).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- Indigenous nations and customary land-holding communities.
- Land law, which decides whether community tenure is recognized.

**What would count against it:** If long-run studies show the short-term forest gains from community titling disappear within a decade, tenure alone is not enough and the monitoring role needs separate evidence.

**Directory coverage:** 7 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 2,040 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, GB, US.

City-level coverage is not published for this circuit because the work involves people at risk.

## Community energy transition

**Goal on the map:** Start a community energy project  
**Evidence:** Parts documented separately. Citizen ownership at scale is well documented. The role of local sustainability groups in starting energy co-ops is not source-checked here.

Community-owned generation keeps energy income local, but it needs an organization to own and run it, capital on patient terms, and a stable price or support scheme.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find energy experience (community energy group or energy cooperative) | Ask what it has built, how members invest and what it earns per unit. | 245 | 51 |
| Find capital (credit union or cooperative lender) | Ask whether it finances community shares or small generation projects. | 188 | 11 |
| Find local organizers (local transition or sustainability group) | Ask whether the group has an active energy project or only an interest. | 497 | 800 |

**Where it has been done**

- **REScoop.eu** (Europe). The federation reports a network of 2,500 energy communities representing over 2 million citizens. The figure is self-reported. [Source](https://www.rescoop.eu/about-us/), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Citizen-owned renewables** (Germany). Private individuals and farmers owned 40.4% of installed renewable capacity in 2019, down from 42% in 2016 and more than half about a decade earlier. [Source](https://www.unendlich-viel-energie.de/studie-buergerenergie-bleibt-zentrale-saeule-der-energiewende), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- In the United Kingdom, closure of the feed-in tariff made the most prominent community energy business model unviable; 97% of new community capacity in 2019 had depended on it. [Source](https://www.communityenergyengland.org/files/document/484/1615989181_CommunityEnergy-StateoftheSector2020Report.pdf).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- The grid operator and the national support scheme or price rules.

**What would count against it:** This circuit bears on CLAIMS.md C2. If community energy organizations formed before a subsidy withdrawal mostly stop building or dissolve within five years of it, commons-based provision here depends on policy more than the framework says.

## Cooperative rural broadband

**Goal on the map:** Bring fast internet to an underserved rural area  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

Commercial providers often skip sparse rural areas. Member-owned utilities already have poles, rights of way and customers, and some have added fibre.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find a member-owned utility (community energy group or energy cooperative) | Ask whether it has studied fibre and how it would finance it. | 245 | 51 |
| Find public partners (anchor institution (hospital, university, public body)) | Ask whether the council or hospital would be an early customer or guarantor, and what risk that carries. | 1,785 | 60 |
| Find public access and digital skills (library or community learning centre) | Ask whether it offers public connections and training. | 2,199 | 28 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Rural electric cooperatives building fibre** (United States). More than 109 rural electric co-ops had started fibre projects by 2020, and co-ops provided about 30% of the fibre service available in rural areas. The source is an advocacy organization. [Source](https://ilsr.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/2020_05_19_Rural-Co-op-Report.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- RS Fiber, a Minnesota broadband co-op backed by city bonds, could not make its bond payments in 2018 and member cities raised local taxes to cover a shortfall of about $1.07 million over two years. [Source](https://www.nujournal.com/news/local-news/2018/12/02/taxpayers-asked-to-pony-up-for-rs-fiber-shortfall/).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- Public broadband grants and the rules for pole access.

**What would count against it:** If take-up in a planned area is too low to service the debt without public guarantees, the project transfers risk to taxpayers, as at RS Fiber.

## Disaster resilience grid

**Goal on the map:** Prepare neighbours and services before a disaster  
**Evidence:** Parts documented separately

After a disaster, help moves through relationships that already exist. Neighbourhood groups know who needs what, coordinating bodies hold logistics, and clinics provide care.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find neighbourhood networks (neighbourhood mutual aid network) | Ask whether the group is still active and what it would do in an emergency. | 5,164 | 4,911 |
| Find coordinating bodies (disaster preparedness or relief coordinator) | Ask how unaffiliated volunteers and local groups are included in plans. | 217 | 22 |
| Find clinical capacity (community clinic or health centre) | Ask what it can provide if power or transport fails. | 900 | 20 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Occupy Sandy** (New York, United States). A study prepared for the Department of Homeland Security estimated the volunteer network grew to about 60,000 people at its peak, more than four times the number deployed by the American Red Cross. The report notes the count is hard to estimate reliably. [Source](https://mirror.explodie.org/the-resilient-social-network.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- A review of research on social capital and recovery notes that tight local networks are double-edged; strong groups can exclude outsiders from help. [Source](https://blogs.lse.ac.uk/lsereviewofbooks/2013/02/14/book-review-building-resilience-social-capital-in-post-disaster-recovery).
- The directory lists 4,145 mutual aid records from one 2020 wiki. Their current activity is unknown. [Source](https://github.com/simonlpaige/commonweave/blob/master/docs/DATA-AUDIT-2026-09-05.md).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- Public emergency management, which controls access, funding and official information.

**What would count against it:** If fewer than one in five listed mutual aid groups in a pilot locality can be reached, the directory cannot support this circuit there.

## Eldercare commons

**Goal on the map:** Help older neighbours stay at home  
**Evidence:** Parts documented separately

Ageing at home depends on everyday practical help, social contact, paid care when needed and reachable clinical care.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find older people's organizations (older people's support organization) | Ask what members need most and who is left out. | 2,009 | 107 |
| Find neighbour exchange (time bank or neighbour exchange) | Ask how many active members it has and what cannot be exchanged. | 3 | 3 |
| Find paid care (home-care provider or carers' organization) | Ask about cost, waiting times and worker conditions. | 119 | 60 |
| Find clinical care (community clinic or health centre) | Ask about home visits and transport. | 900 | 20 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Village model of member-run ageing support** (United States and elsewhere). The movement that began with Beacon Hill Village in Boston now counts approximately 350 villages. [Source](https://www.beaconhillvillage.org/pages/10062-village-to-village-network), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- Japan's Fureai Kippu time-credit schemes fell from 132 in 2005 to 95 in 2008, and the researcher concludes no universal panacea can be expected from time banking in eldercare. [Source](https://www.ijccr.net/article/view/9150).
- Only three release records match the time bank rule, so that role will nearly always appear missing. [Source](https://github.com/simonlpaige/commonweave/blob/master/SOLUTION-CIRCUITS.md).

**What would count against it:** If neighbour exchange cannot be shown to reduce paid-care hours or loneliness measures in a pilot, keep it as social contact and stop presenting it as care provision.

## Cooperative development pipeline

**Goal on the map:** Set up cooperative development support  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

New cooperatives need advice from people who have done it, finance that accepts their ownership model, and training in running a member-owned business.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find cooperative experience (cooperative developer, federation or support network) | Ask about formation, governance and support for your sector. | 581 | 90 |
| Find cooperative finance (credit union or cooperative lender) | Ask what it lends to start-ups and on what security. | 188 | 11 |
| Build skills together (workforce training or apprenticeship provider) | Ask whether training is open to your members. | 142 | 5 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Mutual funds for cooperative development** (Italy). Law 59/1992 requires cooperatives affiliated to the national associations to pay 3% of annual profits into funds that promote and finance new cooperatives. [Source](https://www.diritto.it/i-fondi-mutualistici-per-la-promozione-e-lo-sviluppo-della-cooperazione/), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Co-op Cincy** (Cincinnati, United States). Began as the Cincinnati Union Co-op Initiative and has incubated or supported over a dozen co-ops employing more than 100 workers, with finance from a cooperative loan network. [Source](https://seedcommons.org/projects/building-a-cooperative-economy-in-cincinnati), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- A review of worker co-op research finds they survive at least as long as other firms, but notes much of the survival evidence comes from countries whose co-op law prevents the usual failure modes. [Source](https://base.socioeco.org/docs/worker_co-op_report.pdf).
- At Mondragon, depending on the sector, only 32% to 45% of workers were owner-members in 2019. Growth has come with a large non-member workforce. [Source](https://dare.uva.nl/id/b3080656-1109-4b7e-b5c1-fa68b007dada).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- Cooperative law and tax treatment, which differ sharply between countries.

**What would count against it:** If co-ops started through a local pipeline fail at the same rate as other small firms in that place, the support roles are not adding survival and should be redesigned.

## Community school hub

**Goal on the map:** Support children and families through a school  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

Schools are where families already go. Bringing health care, food and family services into the school can raise attendance, if partners stay.

> **Care needed.** Children's information must never be collected or shared through this directory.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find the school community (school or school community) | Ask what families say they need and who decides what happens on site. | 5,641 | 115 |
| Find health partners (community clinic or health centre) | Ask whether it can run sessions at the school. | 900 | 20 |
| Find food partners (food bank or free-food program) | Ask whether it can supply a school pantry without stigma. | 2,202 | 91 |
| Find counselling (mental health or addiction service) | Ask about waiting times and parental consent. | 1,656 | 308 |

**Where it has been done**

- **New York City Community Schools Initiative** (New York, United States). A RAND evaluation found a positive impact on attendance in all grades across all three study years, and on graduation in two of three years. [Source](https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RR3245.html), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- The same evaluation found no significant effect on reading in any year, on maths in the first two years, or on family engagement. The design was quasi-experimental. [Source](https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RR3245.html).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- The school district or education authority that funds the coordinator post.

**What would count against it:** If attendance does not improve within two years of adding partners, the partnership is not reproducing the evaluated result.

## Participatory budgeting

**Goal on the map:** Give residents a say over part of a public budget  
**Evidence:** Combination documented

Residents know local needs but rarely decide spending. Participatory budgeting gives them a defined share to allocate, which requires a public body to commit money and local groups to bring people in.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find the public body (anchor institution (hospital, university, public body)) | Ask what share of which budget could be opened, and whether results would be binding. | 1,785 | 60 |
| Find neighbourhood organizers (neighbourhood or civic association) | Ask who usually does not take part and how to reach them. | 3,498 | 137 |
| Find a neutral venue and information (library or community learning centre) | Ask whether it can host meetings and publish proposals. | 2,199 | 28 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Participatory budgeting in large Brazilian cities** (Brazil). Adoption was associated with an estimated 11% decrease in infant mortality and a 6% increase in health and sanitation spending. The study is observational. [Source](https://www.oidp.net/docs/repo/doc402.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Participatory Budgeting World Atlas 2019** (Worldwide). Counted between 11,690 and 11,825 participatory budgeting processes. These are processes, not cities, and many exist because national law requires them. [Source](https://npms.paginas.ufsc.br/files/2019/12/Atlas-2019-Web.pdf), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- The Brazilian association was stronger under one party's mayors, a possible confound the authors acknowledge. [Source](https://www.oidp.net/docs/repo/doc402.pdf).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- The elected council that must agree to share budget authority.

**What would count against it:** If participants in a local process are less representative of the area than voters in the last local election, the process is concentrating influence, not spreading it.

**Directory coverage:** 22 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 2,189 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, BR, CA, GB, US.

## Community oversight of technology

**Goal on the map:** Give workers and residents a say over AI and surveillance tools  
**Evidence:** Parts documented separately. Union bargaining and local oversight ordinances are each documented. The sources do not show them combined, and voluntary public-input exercises have not been shown to change company decisions.

Decisions about automated systems are mostly made by vendors and employers. Bargaining and local law are the two routes that have produced binding limits so far.

| Role | What to ask | Release records | Map points |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Find worker representation (labor union) | Ask whether automation or monitoring is covered in any agreement. | 842 | 506 |
| Find legal and rights expertise (civil-liberties or digital-rights organization) | Ask whether it has drafted or reviewed a local oversight ordinance. | 35 | 4 |
| Find residents' organizations (neighbourhood or civic association) | Ask which public technologies residents are worried about. | 3,498 | 137 |

**Where it has been done**

- **Writers Guild of America 2023 agreement** (United States). The union's summary states that AI cannot write or rewrite literary material, AI output is not source material, and a company cannot require a writer to use AI software. [Source](https://www.wgacontract2023.org/the-campaign/summary-of-the-2023-wga-mba), checked 2026-11-26.
- **Community Control Over Police Surveillance laws** (United States). The sponsoring organization reports such laws adopted in 26 jurisdictions covering nearly 18 million people. The count is self-reported and undated. [Source](https://www.aclu.org/community-control-over-police-surveillance), checked 2026-11-26.

**What went wrong or remains unproven**

- Driver's Seat, a data cooperative for gig workers, has been wound down and its work absorbed into a university project. The data co-op form has not yet shown durability. [Source](https://wao.cs.princeton.edu/).
- A study of one company's public-input program identifies unspoken assumptions, such as that participation must be scalable, that limit what such exercises can decide. [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.11613).

**Needed, but not something the directory can find**

- Legislatures and regulators. Most binding rules on AI come from law, not from community organizations.

**What would count against it:** If oversight ordinances are adopted but audits show agencies acquire tools without the required approval, the circuit produces paper rules only.

**Directory coverage:** 2 recorded cities have a match for every role, out of 1,726 with a match for at least one. Countries with every role: AU, GB, US.

Cities with the most candidates per role, as leads for a closer look: Chicago, IL (US); New York, NY (US).

**Related open problems:** [ai-governance](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#ai-governance), [transparency-limits](OPEN-PROBLEMS.md#transparency-limits)

## Role rules

Each role is recognised from published fields only: organization model, source list, registration type, tags, United States NTEE activity code, and whole-word phrases in the name. The rules are in [`data/circuits.yaml`](data/circuits.yaml) and the matcher is [`data/circuit_match.py`](data/circuit_match.py). The map has fewer fields than the release, so it finds fewer candidates.

Sample check: On 2026-11-26 one AI reviewer read up to ten rule matches per role, drawn by `python data/build_circuits.py --sample 10` and spread across sources, and judged from the name alone whether the record plausibly performs the role. Ten names per role is a rough signal, not a measured precision, and no organization was contacted or looked up.

Notes from the sample check:

- **Self-build or sweat-equity housing program:** Almost all matches are Habitat for Humanity affiliates; the same international filing name appears on many United States rows.
- **Nonprofit affordable-housing developer:** NTEE housing codes also cover housing co-ops and tenant groups.
- **Tenant or resident organization:** Only 21 release records match. Tenant unions are nearly absent from the directory.
- **Legal aid or community law centre:** NTEE legal-services codes include mediation and advocacy groups.
- **Labor union:** United States matches are mostly joint labor-management funds filed under the labor-union code, not union locals; the directory holds almost no locals. The Wikidata union list also contains non-unions, including a learned society and a religious group.
- **Worker cooperative:** Three of ten sampled rows were the same organization from different sources.
- **Cooperative developer, federation or support network:** Membership lists of cooperative networks include ordinary co-ops and a row parsed from research prose.
- **Workforce training or apprenticeship provider:** NTEE employment codes and the phrase "training centre" bring in unrelated education groups.
- **Anchor institution (hospital, university, public body):** Weak rule. Most matches are groups attached to a hospital or university (appeals, student bodies, clinics), not the institution. Treat as a prompt to look up the institution itself.
- **Community health worker or health-education group:** Includes clinics and research institutes filed under public-health codes.
- **Home-care provider or carers' organization:** Includes support groups for unpaid family carers as well as care providers.
- **Time bank or neighbour exchange:** Only three release records match.
- **Neighbourhood mutual aid network:** Older fraternal and insurance-style mutual aid societies match the phrase. Most records date from 2020 and current activity is unknown.
- **Food cooperative, hub or market:** Only 34 release records match.
- **Conservation or watershed steward:** "Conservation trust" also names building-preservation charities, and environmental-justice groups share the NTEE codes.
- **Community energy group or energy cooperative:** Transition groups tagged with an energy interest are counted; they may have no generation project.
- **Mediation or restorative-justice organization:** Includes commercial arbitration chambers and family mediation.
- **Community violence-prevention or survivor-support group:** The youth-violence NTEE code is applied loosely in the source data.
- **Community media outlet:** Matches are almost all in Australia and Brazil.
- **Library or community learning centre:** About seven in ten matches are Bulgarian chitalishta (community cultural centres with libraries).
- **School or school community:** The word "school" appears in many names that are not schools or school communities.
- **Civil-liberties or digital-rights organization:** Only 35 release records match.

## Adding or changing a circuit

1. Edit `data/circuits.yaml`. A precedent needs a public source you opened yourself and the date you opened it.
2. Add at least one limit: a failure, a null result, or a condition the precedent depended on.
3. Write a falsifier that names something a third party could observe.
4. Run `python data/build_circuits.py`, then `python data/build_circuits.py --check` and the test suites.
5. If a rule looks wrong, sample it with `python data/build_circuits.py --sample 10` and record what you find in `data/audit/circuit-role-precision.json`.
